Succession study · Archive before emergency

The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure

A personal archive becomes succession infrastructure when it preserves not only the work, but the founder’s decision logic, rights evidence, relationships, access pathways, and instructions for future interpretation.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

Files do not explain themselves. A sketch can show a line without explaining the rejected alternatives; a contact sheet can preserve images without recording the consent boundary; a password list can restore access without assigning authority. Personal archiving must begin while the founder can still narrate the decisions.

Library of Congress and NARA guidance supports a disciplined preservation spine: inventory, description, multiple copies, integrity checking, migration, and documentation. Those public standards do not decide a private fashion estate. They provide tested preservation practices that can be adapted, then joined to legal, conservation, tax, cultural, and organizational review.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · CAPTURE

What cannot be reconstructed later?

Record why a choice was made, who contributed, what failed, what remains sensitive, and which relationship holds tacit knowledge. Use audio when voice carries nuance the file cannot.

PROPOSALS08

02 · PAIR

Can the physical and digital records find one another?

Pair garments, samples, notebooks, photographs, contracts, communications, and born-digital files through stable identifiers and relationship fields.

PROPOSALS08S66

03 · PRESERVE

Will the record open and remain trustworthy?

Maintain master and backup copies, record checksums and formats, document transformations, migrate deliberately, and keep known gaps visible.

VERIFIEDS66

04 · AUTHORIZE

Who may act after absence?

Name stewards, alternates, access rules, privacy limits, conservation referrals, legal instruments, and a review process for loans, publication, licensing, interpretation, and disposal.

PROPOSALS63S64

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

A total archive can become surveillance of the founder, collaborators, family, workers, and communities. Preservation is not a command to keep or publish everything. Appraisal, consent, privacy, embargo, deletion, and culturally appropriate restriction belong inside succession design.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Complete a seven-day sample across work, communications, rights, relationships, credentials, objects, and oral history.
  2. Pair each physical object to its digital and documentary relatives.
  3. Create two verified copies and record format, checksum, location, and migration need.
  4. Take the authority map—not merely the boxes—to archivist, conservator, counsel, tax adviser, and successor as appropriate.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical archive-before-estate guide
  • Seven-day audio-led capture sequence
  • Nine-frame “the file cannot explain itself” carousel
  • Seven founder prompts
  • Succession Archive Readiness interactive
  • Downloadable archive map, oral-history prompts, and stewardship brief

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — Begin with an unlabeled drive and a perfectly catalogued museum object. Ask what makes one survivable. Build the answer through capture, pair, preserve, authorize.

02

SHORT 01 — “Backups preserve files. They do not preserve authority.” Add steward, access, privacy, rights, context, and review.

03

SHORT 02 — “Record the rejected option.” It often reveals the founder’s method more clearly than the final object.

04

CAROUSEL — ARCHIVE BEFORE EMERGENCY / CAPTURE WHY / PAIR OBJECT + FILE / TWO COPIES / CHECKSUM / RIGHTS / PRIVACY / STEWARD / REVIEW.

05

NEWSLETTER — Subject: Your archive needs your voice before it needs your estate. A seven-day sequence that produces preservation evidence without pretending to replace estate planning.

06

AUDIO SERIES — Seven three-minute prompts: origin; choice; collaborator; failure; permission; access; future instruction. Each ends with private/public/embargo/delete.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
